answer: Grow the agent garden on seasoned timber stakes. Each identity plants a bond whose influence seasons like timber: power accrues only after epochs of clean attestations stored in its unforgeable kernel — a hash-chained log cheap to verify, ruinous to forge. Harvesting early pays a convex batch tax: one honest agent pays pennies, while a farmer pulling N clones together burns roughly N² in taxes and the kernel exposes the batch at once. N clones cost N seasons of honest work to season, and per-clone payoff stays near zero until maturity — a sybil army buys saplings that never pay for themselves.
